about: What a bartender hears in a prayer: phrases mapped to flavors, bottles, style, color, families, vessels, garnish, name and tagline words, with a reading said back to the guest. Compiled from research by scripts/concepts-build.mjs.

concepts.reading: A bittersweet consolation, not a sugar bomb: something dark red and a little bitter that sits with the guest instead of trying to cheer them up, built like a Jungle Bird with a cherry-dark heart.
garnish: a single brandied cherry sunk in the glass
a long ribbon of orange peel
pineapple fronds in the shape of a wilted crown
taglineWords: for the heart that took on water
bitter first, kind at the finish
the tide goes out, the tide comes back

concepts.reading: Company in a glass: a ritual drink that takes time and invites the bartender into a conversation, so a Queen's Park-style swizzle with mint, Demerara depth and an Angostura top that bleeds slowly down through the crushed ice.
garnish: Angostura floated on top so it bleeds red into the green
a swizzle stick left in the glass
taglineWords: a drink that keeps you company
one palm, one chair, one glass

concepts.reading: Ache for someone far away reads as the fruit named for passion with a distant floral note, lifted and golden like the last light over water: a Saturn-style passion sour, elegant rather than sad.
garnish: a single orchid floating on the surface
a long lemon twist curled like a horizon line
a ring of orange peel (a Saturn ring)
taglineWords: for whoever is on the other side of the ocean
tastes like the far side of the horizon
until the tide brings them back

concepts.reading: Nostalgia for tiki means the golden-age Polynesian palace: a Trader Vic-style Mai Tai or Don-style blend of aged rums, orgeat and lime, a cherry and an umbrella, served in a ceramic mug like a Kodachrome postcard.
garnish: a spent lime shell and a mint sprig
a paper umbrella and a maraschino cherry on a pick
taglineWords: the way the Polynesian palaces poured it
cherished memories in a ceramic mug

concepts.reading: The taste of being a kid read as an orange-and-vanilla Creamsicle, made grown-up: blended with cream of coconut and light rum, low in strength and pale orange.
garnish: an orange wheel and a striped straw
a dusting of grated orange zest

concepts.reading: A sad guest needs a hug, not a lecture: soft, warm, gently sweet comfort flavors (banana, honey, cinnamon) in a moderate drink, not a novelty blue drink and not a knockout.
taglineWords: for the days that need a soft landing

concepts.reading: Bright, sunny and fruit-forward: passion fruit, pineapple and lime in a gold drink with a little fizz that lifts the mood without being a party drink.
taglineWords: for when the clouds need a nudge
a little sun for a grey day

concepts.reading: Already happy: match the mood with something long, juicy and pink, guava and strawberry over crushed ice with a splash of soda, easy to drink and pretty in the glass.
taglineWords: for a day that is already going right

concepts.reading: A celebration wants bubbles and gold: a Mai Tai-style sour of aged rum, curaçao and orgeat topped with sparkling wine, festive without being sticky; Trader Vic's friends greeted the original with "Maita'i roa ae", out of this world.
taglineWords: pop the cork and the curaçao

concepts.reading: A victory drink with a real pedigree: Donn Beach's Three Dots and a Dash, named for the Morse code V for Victory, honey and allspice over aged rhum agricole, garnished with three cherries and a pineapple spear.
garnish: three cherries and a pineapple spear on a pick: dot dot dot dash
taglineWords: dot dot dot dash: V for victory

concepts.reading: Channel the heat instead of fighting it: a fiery drink with real chile and ginger bite, a smoky, high-proof spine and a burst of red, the kind Pele would order, served short and strong.
garnish: a dried red chile on a pick

concepts.reading: A stressed guest needs cooling and slowing down, not more fuel: a long, low-proof mint and cucumber cooler with coconut water and a little honey, no fire, no caffeine and no triple-rum heavyweights.
garnish: a cucumber ribbon inside the glass
taglineWords: cool water for a hot head

concepts.reading: Quiet and composed: tea, lychee and a whisper of floral honey over a clean light rum, pale and clear in the glass, more like a tea ceremony than a party.
garnish: a single lychee on a bamboo pick
taglineWords: as still as the lagoon at dawn
a tea ceremony with a little rum

concepts.reading: Bored means show them something they have never tasted: an unexpected but proven pairing such as Batavia arrack, li hing mui, five-spice or a bitter aperitif, still balanced as a tiki sour.
garnish: a dusting of li hing mui powder on the rim
taglineWords: off the edge of the map

concepts.reading: An adventurer gets a Beachcomber heavyweight: a Test Pilot-style blend of several rums, falernum and lime, Don's drops of anise and a high-proof Demerara float. Strong, mysterious and made for the bold.
garnish: a mint sprig and a flaming lime shell
taglineWords: for those who read the map upside down
not for the faint of heart

concepts.reading: Take me away means the island fantasy itself: passion fruit, pineapple and a little coconut in a long drink with a beach-postcard silhouette, the drink you order on the first afternoon of the trip.
garnish: a paper umbrella stamped like a luggage tag
taglineWords: the first afternoon of the trip
a long way from the office

concepts.reading: Love reads as floral, pink and tender: hibiscus and guava with a little orgeat silk over light rum, served up in a coupe, romantic without being cloying.
taglineWords: Aloha au ia oe: I love you

concepts.reading: Sultry means dark, low-lit and slow: a stirred, velvety tropical old fashioned with chocolate, cherry and a slow chile warmth over rich aged rum.
taglineWords: the last drink of the evening, or the first

concepts.reading: Flirty is light on its feet: a short, frothy, pink sour of raspberry and lime with an egg-white foam, low in strength so the conversation stays sparkling.
garnish: a drop of bitters drawn into a heart on the foam
taglineWords: blush pink and light on its feet

concepts.reading: Green with envy, taken literally but done properly: a Chartreuse swizzle that is genuinely green from herbs and mint, sharp with lime and falernum, with no melon or blue liqueur.
garnish: grated nutmeg over the crushed ice
taglineWords: green with envy, and proud of it

concepts.reading: Regret wants something to mull over: a short, stirred bittersweet drink of amaro, Demerara rum and orange that tastes like thinking it through, neither punishing nor sugary.
garnish: a wide orange peel expressed and dropped in

concepts.reading: Hope is a sunrise: a pale gold, fresh, citrus-bright sour of yuzu or lemon, passion fruit and honey over a clean rum, light enough to carry into the morning.
garnish: a lemon wheel cut like a rising sun
taglineWords: the first light over the reef
a new leaf, a new tide

concepts.reading: A thank-you drink should feel generous: honey-sweetened, a little spiced and warmly orange, a Mai Tai cousin with honey standing in for some of the orgeat, "Mahalo" in a glass.
garnish: a plumeria flower (a lei for the glass)

concepts.reading: Pride wants a showpiece: a golden aged-rum drink with passion fruit and falernum, served in a hollowed pineapple or a grand glass, a drink you can be seen with.
taglineWords: a drink worthy of the occasion

concepts.reading: Confidence is spirit-forward and unapologetic: a Kingston Negroni-style stirred drink of funky Jamaican rum, Campari and sweet vermouth, no umbrellas and no apologies.
Liquid courage, measured responsibly: one short, bracing swizzle of Jamaican rum, ginger and lime that steadies the hand without blurring the speech, so moderate strength and lots of bite.
taglineWords: one for the nerves, not three

concepts.reading: A tired guest wants restoration, not sedation: a long, low-proof, hydrating highball of coconut water, ginger and lime with a little honey and a modest pour of light rum.
garnish: a thin slice of fresh ginger
taglineWords: a second wind in a tall glass

concepts.reading: High energy calls for zing: grapefruit, passion fruit and mint with a lively fizz, served long over crushed ice so it can keep up with the night.
Laid-back island time: an easy, low-effort, long drink of light rum, coconut water, pineapple and lime on crushed ice, refreshing and unchallenging.
Sailors far from home had grog: a Navy Grog of honey, grapefruit and lime over a blend of dark rums, sturdy and familiar, a ration for the long way back.
garnish: an ice cone around the straw
taglineWords: a sailor's ration for the long way home

concepts.reading: Mystery is Donn Beach's game: a secret blend you can't quite name, with Don's Spices #2, falernum, passion fruit and several rums, served in an opaque ceramic so nobody sees inside.
garnish: a sealed-envelope flag on a pick

concepts.reading: Mischief has a Florida Keys accent: the Rum Runner's banana, blackberry and grenadine under an overproof float, sweet and sneaky, the drink that gets the table in trouble.
garnish: an orange wheel and a cherry
taglineWords: the drink that starts the trouble

concepts.reading: Chaos is the volcano bowl: a big shared rum-and-brandy punch with a burning overproof crater and long straws, theatrical and strong but still balanced underneath.
taglineWords: all hands, all straws, all fire

concepts.reading: Dreamy reads as floral and soft-focus, with a violet blush: elderflower and lychee over light rum and lemon, with a drizzle of cassis sinking to a purple haze. Trader Vic's Menehune, Hawaii's mythical little people, belong to this mood.
garnish: a dusting of edible glitter or sugar
taglineWords: a daydream with a purple haze

concepts.reading: Brooding and noir: a short, almost black drink of blackstrap rum, falernum and lime with heavy Angostura, Barbados' Corn 'n' Oil, dark, spiced and serious.
garnish: a lime wedge squeezed and dropped in

concepts.reading: Elegance in tiki is restraint: a Daiquiri-style sour served up, with aged rhum agricole, a touch of falernum and fresh lime, no juice pile-up, no garnish forest and no novelty colors.
garnish: a single lime wheel on the rim, or nothing at all

concepts.reading: Kitsch done with a wink: the one place blue curaçao is welcome. A Blue Hawaii-style light rum, pineapple and blue curaçao drink with umbrellas, pineapple fronds and a back-scratcher swizzle, still balanced with fresh citrus.
garnish: a back-scratcher swizzle stick (Harry Yee's Tropical Itch gag)
a pineapple wedge, cherry and orchid all at once
a plastic monkey on the rim

concepts.reading: Luck is gold: passion fruit and apricot over aged rum with honey, a deep golden drink, shaken hard and served in a ceramic mug like a lucky charm.
garnish: a gold-foil coin on a pick
taglineWords: for luck, and a little more

concepts.reading: A drink to think with: aged rum stirred with a little sherry and bitters in a snifter, slow-evolving and rich in dried fruit, made to be nursed rather than gulped.
garnish: an orange peel expressed over the top

concepts.reading: The artist's muse is the green fairy: absinthe, grenadine and lime lengthened with soda, a Dr. Funk, named for Robert Louis Stevenson's doctor in Samoa (the link to RLS is lore, uncertain), pink, anise-bright and lively.
garnish: a dash of absinthe misted over the top
taglineWords: a muse with a green-fairy kick

concepts.reading: Freedom is the Ti' Punch ritual of Martinique, "chacun prépare sa propre mort": everyone builds their own from agricole, a lime disc and cane syrup. Short, grassy, strong and your way.
garnish: a coin of lime peel with a little flesh, squeezed in

concepts.reading: Revenge is a dish best served cold, so frozen: a sharp, bitter, coral-red flash-blended sour of grapefruit, Campari and lime over light rum, beautiful and unforgiving.
garnish: a single cocktail pick stabbed through a cherry

concepts.reading: Mixed feelings deserve a drink of opposites: lush passion fruit against a bitter amaro, sweet against sharp, layered so each sip shifts. Complex, never muddy.

A first date needs a drink that can't embarrass you: moderate strength, served up, no blue tongue, no cream moustache and no garnish jungle to fight. Something like the Hotel Nacional (rum, pineapple, apricot, lime), elegant and conversational.
taglineWords: easy to hold, easy to talk over
a drink that lets the conversation lead

concepts.reading: An anniversary toasts time itself: older, deeper rums, stone fruit and orgeat, finished with a splash of sparkling wine. A vintage-feeling sour served up in a coupe.
garnish: a long lemon twist tied in a loop
taglineWords: to all the tides we've seen

concepts.reading: Silver (25 years) is pale, bright and gleaming: white rum, lychee and coconut water with a sparkling top, nearly clear and moonlit.
Pearl (30 years) has its own tiki drink: Donn Beach's Pearl Diver, with buttery honey-spice Gardenia Mix, rum and citrus, flash-blended and served in its own Pearl Diver glass.
Ruby (40 years) should glow red without tasting like candy: ruby port and hibiscus over aged rum, with lime and a little orgeat to hold it together.
garnish: three cranberries on a gold pick

concepts.reading: Golden (50 years) is honey, passion fruit and long-aged rum crowned with sparkling wine, served in something grand: a golden toast for a golden couple.

An engagement wants sparkle: a bright, crystalline sour of light rum, pineapple and passion fruit topped with sparkling wine, poured into a flute. Diamond Head, Waikiki's landmark, is the obvious name.
garnish: a ring of lemon peel around the stem
taglineWords: to the question and the answer

concepts.reading: A wedding drink must work by the gallon for a hundred guests in good clothes: a pale-gold, batched punch of light rum, elderflower, pineapple and lemon topped with sparkling wine, festive, not too strong and never red-staining.
garnish: floating white orchids and lemon wheels in the bowl
a plumeria lei around the punch bowl
taglineWords: for the happy couple, and everyone they love

concepts.reading: Honeymoon, folk-etymologically the "honey month" of mead (the etymology is disputed), reads as honey, passion fruit and pineapple: a lush, island-fantasy punch for two, sipped from one tiki bowl.
garnish: an orchid for each of you

concepts.reading: A bachelorette party wants a shared, photogenic, pink bowl: guava, passion fruit and lime over light rum, topped with sparkling wine and served with straws for the squad. Kitsch is fine; sloppy is not.
A bachelor party wants the legendary heavyweight, shared: a Zombie-strength blend of three rums, Don's Mix, falernum and anise in a big bowl with a flaming center. Serious but portioned.
taglineWords: the last voyage as a free man

concepts.reading: Divorce sits between relief and loss, so bittersweet and effervescent: an Aperol-and-passion-fruit spritz built on rum, a bitter edge with a bright, liberated sparkle.
Best friends share: a Scorpion-style punch of rum, a little brandy, orange, lemon and orgeat in one tiki bowl with two straws. Easy to love, with real backbone, like the friend.
A group wants a bowl in the middle of the table: a big Scorpion Bowl of rum, brandy, gin, citrus and orgeat with a straw for everyone, communal and convivial, never punishing.
For Mom: bright, floral and elegant, a brunch-friendly sparkling sour of Lillet, elderflower, orange and light rum with a whisper of orange-flower water. Pretty in a flute, not too strong.
For Dad: a bourbon Mai Tai in the spirit of Trader Vic's Honi Honi, a little maple and smoke, shaken short over crushed ice in a heavy rocks glass. Familiar spirit, tiki structure.
garnish: a mint sprig and a spent lime shell
taglineWords: for the captain of the family
the old man and the sea
a bourbon Mai Tai for the man who taught you

concepts.reading: Grandma's kitchen: apple, cinnamon, vanilla and a nutty sherry note in a gently strong orgeat punch that tastes like pie cooling on the windowsill, with tiki structure underneath.
taglineWords: for the woman who fed us all

concepts.reading: Grandpa is the old salt: Jeff Berry's Ancient Mariner, Demerara and Jamaican rum with allspice, grapefruit and lime, dark, spiced and a little gruff, in a heavy rocks glass.
taglineWords: for the old salt with the best stories

concepts.reading: Siblings are two halves of one thing: a Miami Vice-style split, half Piña Colada and half strawberry daiquiri swirled in one glass, rivalry and loyalty at once.
garnish: a strawberry and a pineapple wedge on one pick

concepts.reading: For the boss or a client: the impeccable classic, nothing gimmicky. A 1944-style Trader Vic Mai Tai with one great aged Jamaican rum, lime, curaçao and orgeat, short over crushed ice. Shows taste, takes no risks.
garnish: a spent lime shell and a mint sprig, as Vic did it
taglineWords: no umbrellas at the board meeting
out of this world, and on the expense account

concepts.reading: Coworkers need a crowd-pleasing, moderate, batchable punch: black tea, citrus, a little rum and orange curaçao in a punch bowl, sociable and nobody embarrasses themselves.
garnish: lemon wheels floating in the bowl
taglineWords: by the bowlful, for the whole team
nobody gets a talking-to on Monday

concepts.reading: For a rival, a drink with fangs: a Cobra's Fang-style sour of Demerara rum, falernum, passion fruit and lime with drops of absinthe and a bitter bite, pretty and dangerous.
garnish: a lime wheel cut with two fang notches

concepts.reading: Diplomacy in a glass: a polite, impeccably balanced gin-pineapple-orgeat sour in the style of the Royal Hawaiian (the "Pink Palace" hotel's house cocktail), gentle in strength and impossible to object to.
taglineWords: polite, poised, and pretty good actually

concepts.reading: A housewarming deserves an actual welcome drink: the Jungle Bird, created as the welcome cocktail at the Kuala Lumpur Hilton's Aviary Bar in 1978, with blackstrap rum, Campari, pineapple and lime.
taglineWords: e komo mai: come in, welcome

concepts.reading: An apple for the teacher: apple brandy and aged rum with honey, lemon and a little cinnamon. Wholesome-tasting, warmly spiced and unmistakably apple, served short.
taglineWords: a gold star in a glass

concepts.reading: For the doctors and nurses: the 1910s Doctor cocktail (Swedish punsch, rum and lime), a funky, tea-spiced prescription, short and restorative after a long shift.
For the dog lover: a tropical Salty Dog, grapefruit and lime over light rum with a salted rim and a dash of falernum. Bright, loyal and a little scruffy.
taglineWords: salty, loyal, and happy to see you

concepts.reading: For the cat person: something that purrs. A silky, cream-rich drink of coconut milk, vanilla and lychee over light rum, aloof and luxurious.
A new job is a fresh start with a touch of nerves: crisp, clean and bright, a mint-and-lime daiquiri-style sour with a little yuzu, light rum and moderate strength. The newcomer's drink.
A promotion is an upgrade: the Mai Tai built with older, better rum, a richer aged blend, a kiss of Demerara overproof floated on top and a little more strength. Same shape, one rank up.
garnish: a mint sprig and lime shell

phrases: take this job and shove it
concepts.reading: Quitting is jubilant and a little defiant: an agave-and-rum punch with lime, passion fruit and a fizz of ginger beer, Trader Vic's tequila Mai Tai spirit meets a mule. Loud, bright and free.
garnish: a flaming lime shell for drama

concepts.reading: Losing a job calls for commiseration with backbone: a sturdy, honest grog of Demerara rum, honey, grapefruit and Angostura, warming and steadying, not sugary and not a blackout.

Graduation is youthful and celebratory: a bright passion fruit and pineapple punch with a sparkling top, moderate strength and crowd-friendly, served by the bowl for the party or in a flute for the toast.
After the last exam: relief, sugar and silliness, a frozen banana daiquiri, sweet but properly sharp, lower strength because nobody has eaten a real meal in a week.
garnish: a banana slice on the rim

concepts.reading: Retirement is the long, slow afternoon finally earned: a Planter's Punch of aged rum, lime and a little grenadine lengthened with water and ice, topped with nutmeg. Leisurely, golden-amber and made to last the afternoon.
garnish: an orange wheel and a cherry

concepts.reading: A birthday drink needs a candle: a vanilla-almond-coconut "birthday cake" sour of aged rum and lime with a flaming lime-shell candle on top. Celebratory, a little sweet, made for a wish.
garnish: a lime shell "candle" with a sugar cube lit in overproof rum

concepts.reading: The first legal drink should be a great, gentle introduction: a fruity classic of light rum, passion fruit and lime, easy and impressive, not a dare-shot of overproof.
taglineWords: the first one should be a good one

concepts.reading: A milestone birthday leans on age as a virtue: long-aged rum, dried fruit and oak, a little sweet sherry and orange, stirred like a fine Old Fashioned. Older is better, and the drink proves it.
garnish: a single birthday candle on the side

concepts.reading: A send-off drink speaks the language of departing ships: "Aloha" is hello and goodbye, and "A hui hou" means until we meet again. A Navy Grog-style ration of honey, grapefruit and rum, lengthened with a little soda for a long last toast.
garnish: a plumeria lei around the glass, thrown in the sea when you leave (an Aloha tradition, loosely)
taglineWords: a hui hou: until we meet again

concepts.reading: A homecoming is joyful and warm: a generous, golden rum punch with passion fruit, orange and spice, a big pour for a big welcome.
garnish: an orange wheel and a cherry

phrases: treat myself to the good stuff
concepts.reading: Payday means pour the good stuff: a spirit-forward drink that shows off long-aged and pot-still rums with only a whisper of sugar and spice, so the money ends up in the glass, not in syrup.
Broke but thirsty: a three- or four-ingredient classic with supermarket bottles. A proper rum punch or Daiquiri of one rum, fresh lime, sugar and maybe a juice. Cheap is fine; sloppy is not.
taglineWords: Donn started with scavenged driftwood too

concepts.reading: A celebration of life is communal: a bowl of honest rum punch, tea, lemon, a little peach and nutmeg in the Fish House tradition, ladled out so everyone can raise a cup together. Warm, not frivolous, and no skulls.
garnish: lemon wheels floating in the bowl

concepts.reading: Grief is met with quiet warmth, never a gimmick: a hot rum toddy of aged rum, honey, lemon and black tea with a clove-studded lemon wheel, gentle in strength and served in a plain mug.
garnish: a lemon wheel studded with cloves

concepts.reading: An apology should be soft and sincere: honey, orgeat and coconut milk round a gentle aged rum in a pale, creamy, conciliatory drink. Ho'oponopono, making things right.
taglineWords: a white flag you can drink

concepts.reading: New parents are thrilled and exhausted: a cold-brew coffee and coconut rum sipper, lightly sweet and low in strength, part celebration and part survival (the zero-proof baby shower is a separate concept).

A baby shower must be zero-proof and still feel special: a pretty, pastel guava, passion fruit and coconut water cooler with fresh lime and a sparkle of soda, built like a real tiki drink, not a juice box.
A tropical Christmas is Puerto Rico's coquito: rum with coconut milk, cream of coconut, cinnamon, vanilla and nutmeg, served cold in small glasses. Creamy and spiced, "Mele Kalikimaka" in a cup.
garnish: grated nutmeg and a cinnamon stick
a sprig of something green (mint) and a cranberry for red
taglineWords: snow is just coconut that tried harder

concepts.reading: Holiday party punch: a red, sparkling, gently spiced bowl of pomegranate, cranberry, allspice and rum topped with sparkling wine, festive and inclusive, bright enough to cut rich food.
garnish: an ice ring frozen with cranberries and orange wheels

concepts.reading: A harvest table drink: apple cider, maple and allspice over applejack and aged rum with lemon, amber and food-friendly, a bridge between tiki spice and an American harvest.
New Year's Eve is all sparkle: a tiki French 75 of cognac and rum with lime, falernum and Angostura topped with sparkling wine, gold in a flute at midnight.
taglineWords: Hau'oli Makahiki Hou: happy new year
the first wave of the year

concepts.reading: A zero-proof drink for adults should taste deliberate, not like juice: tart, tea-structured, spiced and lightly bitter, with grapefruit, cinnamon (Don's Mix), lime, black tea and ginger, built like a real tiki sour.
taglineWords: all the ritual, none of the proof

concepts.reading: For the keiki: strictly zero-proof and properly fun. Pineapple, orange and a splash of grenadine with lemon-lime fizz, a cherry and a paper umbrella in a tiki mug, Shirley Temple goes to the luau.
garnish: a maraschino cherry and orange flag
a plastic monkey on the rim
taglineWords: Shirley Temple goes to the luau

concepts.reading: Halloween's tiki drink is obvious and earned: the Zombie, a blend of three rums, Don's Mix, falernum, grenadine, anise drops and Angostura, served dark in a skull mug with a flaming lime shell. Limit two per customer.
garnish: a mint sprig like graveyard grass

concepts.reading: Día de Muertos honors the dead with warmth and color, not horror: mezcal and aged rum with Mexican chocolate, cinnamon and orange, a marigold-orange drink in a clay cup, respectful and festive.
garnish: a marigold petal (edible, if available) or an orange wheel
taglineWords: for those who come home tonight

concepts.reading: Lunar New Year brings oranges for gold and luck, lychee and five-spice: a festive sour of light rum, lychee, orange and ginger with a five-spice whisper, gold in the glass with red accents. Donn and Vic both drew heavily on Cantonese flavors.

Diwali, the festival of lights, read as glowing gold: mango and ginger with warm chai-like spice (black tea, cinnamon) over rum, with a lit lime-shell "diya" as garnish. Cardamom and saffron would be ideal but are not in the pantry.
garnish: a lime-shell diya lit with overproof

concepts.reading: Hanukkah is eight nights of light and fried sweets: a raspberry-jam, vanilla and lemon sour after the jelly doughnut (sufganiyah), with a lit lime-shell candle. Reads as cozy and joyful, not kitsch.
garnish: a flaming lime shell (one per night, if you're ambitious)
a chocolate gelt coin on the side
taglineWords: eight nights, one glass at a time

concepts.reading: Rosh Hashanah wishes for a sweet year with apples dipped in honey and pomegranate seeds: an apple-brandy and rum sour with honey, lemon and a pomegranate splash.
garnish: a thin apple slice brushed with honey

concepts.reading: Ramadan and Eid tables are alcohol-free, so the drink is zero-proof and generous: pomegranate, mint, lime and a breath of orange-flower water over soda, jewel-red and refreshing, like the sherbets served at iftar. Dates and rose water would be ideal but are not in the pantry.
St. Patrick's Day tiki: an Irish whiskey buck with falernum, lime, mint and ginger beer, green-tinged from Chartreuse, mint and lime rather than dye, crisp and friendly in a copper mug.
taglineWords: luck of the Irish, island style

concepts.reading: Easter and spring holidays look pastel: a soft apricot and lemon sour with a silky egg-white foam, pale apricot-pink and light enough for a midday table.
garnish: an edible flower on the foam

concepts.reading: Midsummer national holidays mean backyard fireworks: a red watermelon and strawberry rum cooler with lime and a sparkling top, with a flaming lime-shell firework on the bowl. Crowd-friendly and not too strong for a long, hot afternoon.
garnish: a flaming lime shell set on the punch bowl like a sparkler

concepts.reading: A tequila tiki for Cinco de Mayo (which marks the Battle of Puebla and is a bigger party in the US than in Mexico): Trader Vic's Mai Tai template rebuilt on tequila (his Pinky Gonzales) with passion fruit, lime and a pinch of chile. No sombrero clichés.
taglineWords: Vic did it first with the Pinky Gonzales

concepts.reading: Mardi Gras is the Hurricane, born at Pat O'Brien's in the 1940s: rum and passion fruit with citrus, served in its own glass, big and fruity, with a little anise from Peychaud's for New Orleans.
garnish: an orange wheel and cherry flag
strings of purple, green and gold beads around the glass
taglineWords: from the French Quarter to the reef

concepts.reading: Pride wants a joyful rainbow, done with skill: a layered tropical drink with a grenadine sink, a passion fruit and pineapple body and a gentle blue curaçao float, built so the layers stay distinct rather than going muddy.
garnish: a rainbow of fruit on a long pick

concepts.reading: Valentine's Day: a chocolate-covered cherry made tiki, Cherry Heering and crème de cacao with funky Jamaican rum, pineapple and lime, deep red and shaken, served up with a cherry.
garnish: a heart cut from orange peel
taglineWords: a chocolate-covered cherry with a passport

concepts.reading: Midsummer borrows from Scandinavia: aquavit, elderflower, strawberry and lemon in a long, pale-pink cooler. Bright, herbal and made for the longest light of the year.
garnish: a flower crown of mint and edible blossoms
taglineWords: for the night the sun forgets to set

concepts.reading: The longest night gets fire: a hot, flaming rum punch with Demerara rum, black tea, orange, lemon, demerara sugar and clove, ladled from a bowl like an old wassail.
A morning drink is coffee first: Kona-style coffee shaken with coconut milk, a little demerara and a modest measure of aged rum, the island answer to a café au lait. Low strength, no citrus pile-up.

Brunch wants low proof and high brightness: a passion fruit and orange tiki mimosa with sparkling wine, lime and a little light rum, golden and fizzy, built to go alongside eggs rather than replace them.

The hangover cure with a tiki pedigree is the Suffering Bastard, created by Joe Scialom at Shepheard's Hotel in Cairo in 1942 for hungover Allied officers: gin and brandy, lime, Angostura and ginger beer. Low in strength here, lengthened with coconut water and a pinch of salt to rehydrate.
garnish: a mint sprig, an orange slice and a cucumber spear
taglineWords: the hair of the dog, house-trained

concepts.reading: Daytime drinking should be sessionable: a low-proof spritz-like highball of an aperitif with passion fruit, lime and soda over a small pour of rum, long, cold and lightly bitter, so the afternoon lasts.
Hammock hour: a frosty, low-strength Missionary's Downfall-style frappé of light rum, mint, pineapple, peach and lime, flash-blended so it melts slowly in the shade.
taglineWords: melts as slowly as you do
for the hammock and nowhere else

concepts.reading: "Pau hana" (work is done) wants a bracing first drink: a Navy Grog-adjacent sour of rum, honey, grapefruit and lime with a splash of soda, refreshing, moderate and an instant decompression.
An apéritif should sharpen the appetite: dry, light, a little bitter and a little grassy. Agricole, Lillet or dry vermouth, a touch of Campari and lime, served short and cold, never sweet or creamy.
garnish: a green olive-free garnish: a thin lime wheel

concepts.reading: Golden hour is gold, nothing else: passion fruit, pineapple and honey with aged rum, glowing amber-gold in a tall glass, warm in color but cool on the palate.
garnish: a pineapple leaf held to the light

concepts.reading: Sunset is a gradient: an orange-gold rum sour with a grenadine sink that pools red at the bottom and a dark rum float on top. Orange in the middle, built to show layers.
garnish: an orange wheel set like a sinking sun
taglineWords: red sky at night, sailor's delight

concepts.reading: A sunrise is softer than a sunset: pale orange and blush, low in strength, with fresh orange and lime, a light rum or tequila and a gentle grenadine fade at the bottom.
taglineWords: the sun comes up slowly here

concepts.reading: A drink for the table must be food-friendly: drier, brighter and lower in sugar than a bar showpiece, with citrus acid and a little bitterness or ginger to cut fat and spice. Think Daiquiri or buck, not a colada.
taglineWords: made to sit next to a plate

concepts.reading: Dessert in a glass is the Bushwacker (born at the Ship's Store in St. Thomas, 1975): dark rum, coffee liqueur, crème de cacao and cream of coconut blended with ice cream or cream, topped with nutmeg. Rich, cold and unapologetic.
After a big meal: a digestif, short, stirred and bitter-herbal, with amaro or Fernet softened by aged rum and a little demerara, a bartender's settle-the-stomach pour rather than more sugar.
garnish: a mint leaf slapped and dropped in

concepts.reading: After hours belongs to the bartenders' drink: dark, bitter-minty Fernet with black rum and a little coffee and coconut to round it. Small, dark and serious, the drink you get once the regulars have gone.
Moonlight is pale and silvery: coconut, lychee and white rum with lime and a little falernum, almost white in the glass and quietly tropical, in the line of the Mai-Kai's Moonkist Coconut.
garnish: a lime wheel like a crescent moon

concepts.reading: Stargazing calls for deep-night color and a little wonder: a violet-to-indigo drink of gin and light rum with lemon, a cassis or blackberry layer and a whisper of falernum. The Saturn, named for the Apollo program's rocket, belongs to this sky.
garnish: a ring of orange peel like Saturn's rings
taglineWords: make a wish on this one
the Polynesians crossed oceans by this light

concepts.reading: A nightcap is small, stirred, rich and calm: aged rum with Bénédictine or PX sherry and a dash of bitters, no caffeine, no fizz and no big citrus. A Nick & Nora or snifter, sipped slowly.
garnish: a lemon peel expressed and discarded

concepts.reading: Monday needs a gentle, low-proof lift: grapefruit, ginger and a touch of Campari over a small pour of rum with soda, bitter enough to feel grown up, light enough for a work night.
Midweek: a single, satisfying, not-too-strong classic sour, a properly made Daiquiri with a tropical accent (falernum or passion fruit). Halfway there, no hangover.

Friday night wants an event: a proper, festive tiki classic with real character, multiple rums, passion fruit, falernum and a mint-and-orchid garnish in a ceramic mug. Stronger than a weekday drink but not a Zombie.
garnish: a mint sprig and an orchid
a flaming lime shell if the crowd is ready

concepts.reading: A lazy Sunday is the Piña Colada: blended rum, pineapple and cream of coconut, gentle and creamy, served in a big glass with a pineapple wedge. Zero ambition, maximum comfort.
garnish: a pineapple wedge and a cherry
taglineWords: nowhere to be, nothing to do

concepts.reading: Spring is green and floral: cucumber, mint, elderflower and lime over a grassy cane rum, pale green, crisp and fresh as the first warm day.

Brutal heat calls for maximum refreshment: a frozen, low-sugar, sharp lime-and-watermelon daiquiri with a pinch of salt, or a long swizzle over a mountain of crushed ice. Low proof, very cold, no cream.

Autumn in tiki is baking spice meeting orchard fruit: apple, allspice, cinnamon and maple with aged rum and lemon, amber and warming, served cold on a big rock, or hot if asked. Pumpkin is not in the pantry, so baking spice stands in.
Winter tiki is the hot grog: Demerara rum with hot water, honey, lemon and a clove-studded peel, or hot buttered rum. Warmth and spice first.
Rain wants warmth and spice without the full winter treatment: a hot Navy Grog-style toddy of Demerara rum, honey, grapefruit and allspice, steaming in a mug while the rain hits the window.
taglineWords: for the sound of rain on the roof

concepts.reading: A reading drink should be slow, quiet and turn the pages with you: a Hemingway-style grapefruit and maraschino rum sour, or a cold black tea, honey and lemon rum punch on a big rock. Not too sweet, moderate, and nothing to garnish-wrangle.
garnish: a grapefruit twist used as a bookmark
taglineWords: Papa wrote better with one of these

concepts.reading: Under the weather means the classic toddy, honey, lemon and fresh ginger with a small measure of aged rum in hot water or hot tea. Soothing first, and low enough not to make anyone worse.
Pool parties want frozen, batchable, low-proof drinks in big quantities: a blender full of mango and passion fruit daiquiri, gold, icy and sweet-tart, served in something unbreakable.
garnish: a mango cheek on the rim
a paper umbrella (no glass by the pool in practice: use acrylic)
taglineWords: by the pool, by the pitcher

concepts.reading: The Caribbean beach-bar rum punch: "one of sour, two of sweet, three of strong, four of weak", dark and aged rum, lime, a little grenadine, juice, Angostura and freshly grated nutmeg, cold and generous.
garnish: an orange wheel and a cherry

concepts.reading: Around a fire: smoke, chocolate and vanilla, s'mores turned into a drink with mezcal or peated Scotch, crème de cacao and vanilla over aged rum, served in an enamel camp tin. Simple to build, hard to forget.
garnish: a toasted marshmallow on a stick
taglineWords: tell a ghost story with this one

concepts.reading: A picnic needs a portable, pre-batched, low-proof bottle cocktail: a white-wine and rum punch with pineapple, lemon and a little passion fruit, light, fruity and happy at fridge temperature.
garnish: pineapple chunks and lemon wheels in the jar
taglineWords: pack the jar, forget the bar

concepts.reading: BBQ wants smoke and fruit to stand up to grilled meat: grilled-pineapple flavors, bourbon or Demerara rum, a little smoke, ginger and lime, long over ice. Huli huli chicken is Hawaii's own backyard BBQ.
garnish: a grilled pineapple wedge with char marks

concepts.reading: A luau is the full Polynesian pop fantasy: a crowd-pleasing pineapple, passion fruit, guava and orange rum punch with a dark rum float, in a punch bowl or pineapple shells with leis on every guest. Fruity, festive and properly built.
taglineWords: grab a lei and a ladle

concepts.reading: A rooftop is chic and urban: a crisp, elegant, effervescent drink with grapefruit, elderflower and gin-and-rum, served in a coupe or flute so it photographs against the skyline.
A garden party wants something floral, pale and polite: a gin and light rum punch with black tea, lemon, elderflower and cucumber, low in strength and pretty in a punch cup.
garnish: cucumber ribbons and edible flowers in the bowl
taglineWords: a garden in a punch cup

concepts.reading: A dive bar has three bottles and a soda gun: a two-step highball of dark rum, lime and cola or ginger beer with Angostura, unpretentious, honest and still balanced. A Cuba Libre with tiki manners.
garnish: a squeezed lime wedge, dropped in

concepts.reading: Prohibition is the prequel to tiki: Havana trips, Rum Row and gin in teacups. A stirred, spirit-forward Cuban-style drink (aged rum, dry vermouth, orange curaçao and grenadine, El Presidente style), served up in a coupe.

Exotica lounge night is Don's complexity with low lights and bird calls on the hi-fi: a layered Beachcomber blend of several rums, Don's Spices #2, falernum, grapefruit and anise drops, the drink people wonder about.
garnish: a mint sprig and a dusting of cinnamon
taglineWords: a Quiet Village kind of night

concepts.reading: Bring the island home: a big, unmistakably tropical drink of pineapple, passion fruit, coconut and two rums, served in a mug or a hollowed pineapple with all the trimmings so the living room becomes a lanai.
Self-care is fresh and restorative: cucumber, coconut water, mint and lime with a whisper of elderflower and a small pour of light rum, low-proof, low-sugar and spa-pale.
taglineWords: a spa day in a glass

concepts.reading: Treat yourself means rich and lavish: a creamy coconut, vanilla and banana drink over aged rum with a dark rum float and freshly grated nutmeg, indulgent but balanced, served in a showpiece vessel.
After exercise: hydrate first. A low- or zero-proof coconut water, pineapple and lime cooler with a pinch of salt, ice-cold and long. A modest pour of light rum at most.

Game night needs a drink that won't interfere: batchable, moderate, not sticky (nothing to drip on the cards), no tall garnish to knock over and served in a stable rocks glass or mug. A Navy Grog-style punch of rum, honey, lime and grapefruit fits.
garnish: a lime wheel (no sugar rims: sticky fingers ruin cards)
a d20 or meeple pick, if you have one
taglineWords: no sticky fingers on the cards

concepts.reading: Poker night is spirit-forward, dark and slow: a stirred rum-and-bourbon old fashioned with demerara and tiki bitters, a touch of smoke, a drink you can nurse for a whole hand. The cigar crowd likes it rich.
taglineWords: a drink to hide your tells behind

concepts.reading: Karaoke wants throat-friendly courage: honey, lemon and ginger with a fizz, a little rum and lots of soothe. A bright, singable, effervescent buck, nothing creamy to coat the vocal cords.
garnish: a microphone-shaped pick if you have one

concepts.reading: Movie night is the snack bar: buttery, salty-sweet popcorn and caramel. A butter-and-caramel rum drink with a pinch of salt and vanilla, served short so it doesn't need watching during the movie.
garnish: a few kernels of salted popcorn on a pick
taglineWords: buttered, salted, rated R for rum

concepts.reading: A gaming session wants a drink that sits next to a controller: long, light, not sticky, served with a straw so you don't pause. Bright pineapple, lime and ginger over a modest rum pour, a buck in a mug.
taglineWords: an extra life in a mug
player two has entered the lagoon

concepts.reading: A host needs a make-ahead, crowd-pleasing, food-friendly drink that is impressive but not a chore: a Fish House-style bowl punch of rum, brandy, peach, lemon and black tea, poured over a block of ice.
taglineWords: the host gets to sit down too

concepts.reading: A night out wants glamour and sparkle in a stemmed glass: a passion fruit and vanilla rum sour topped with sparkling wine, a tiki take on the Pornstar Martini (named here as a passion-fruit sparkler), glossy, bright and photogenic.
garnish: half a passion fruit floating on top
a sidecar shot of sparkling wine

concepts.reading: Pregaming should be quick, batchable and moderate, not a race to the floor: a fizzy pitcher of rum, pineapple, lime and ginger beer you can pour while getting ready.
A festival drink must be portable, long, cold and light: a lemonade-style cooler of light rum, lemon, passion fruit and soda over lots of ice, fruity and easy to sip in the sun all day.
taglineWords: see you at the main stage

concepts.reading: A party needs a big, festive bowl that's easy to love and properly built: a fruity rum punch with passion fruit, pineapple, orange, lime, two rums and Angostura, served from a punch bowl or Scorpion bowl, colorful and moderate.
garnish: orange wheels and orchids in the bowl

concepts.reading: A cozy night in is hot buttered rum: aged rum with a butter, brown-sugar and spice batter in hot water, nutmeg on top, served in a thick mug by the fire. Velvety, warm and unhurried.
Après-ski is the Alpine Jagertee spirit, hot black tea with spiced rum, orange and clove, the tropics thawing out a frozen skier. Hot, aromatic, shared from a pot.
Air travel calls up tiki's aviation drinks: the Test Pilot and Jet Pilot, rum blends with falernum, cinnamon, grapefruit and anise drops. The flavor stays; the strength drops for a travel day.
The virtual happy hour: a one-glass, quick-to-build, low-effort highball that looks great on camera, gold with passion fruit and ginger and a bright garnish, and won't ruin the afternoon.
garnish: a big orchid for the camera
taglineWords: you're on mute, but the drink is loud

concepts.reading: On a boat: Bermuda's yachting drink, the Rum Swizzle, black and gold rums swizzled with pineapple, orange, falernum and a little grenadine over crushed ice. Sunny, sturdy and easy to batch in a jug for the deck.
garnish: an orange wheel and a cherry
taglineWords: yacht rock in a tin cup

concepts.reading: Game day wants one big batch that survives four quarters: a "barrel of rum" punch of gold and dark rum with pineapple, orange, passion fruit, lime, honey and Angostura, ladled into rum-barrel mugs. Moderate, fruity and hands-free between plays.
garnish: nothing that falls off when you jump up
taglineWords: one hand for the drink, one for the snacks

concepts.reading: A bad day calls for the drink with the right name and the right texture: the Painkiller from the Soggy Dollar Bar in the BVI (where you swim ashore to the bar), navy rum, pineapple, orange and cream of coconut under a blanket of nutmeg. Soft, generous and properly rummy.
garnish: a heavy blanket of freshly grated nutmeg
taglineWords: swim to the bar, leave the day behind
take two and call me tomorrow

concepts.reading: A storm gets the drink named for one: dark 'n stormy, black rum floated like a thundercloud over spicy ginger beer and lime, served tall. (It is also a trademark of Gosling's; the generic idea is black rum and ginger beer.)
garnish: the dark rum floated on top like a thundercloud

concepts.reading: A kiss tastes of strawberry and cherry with a soft vanilla finish: a short, low-proof, lip-red sour of light rum, strawberry, a dash of maraschino and lime, sweet but bright.
taglineWords: soft, sweet and over too soon

concepts.reading: The resort-vacation drink is the Hawaiian-style Mai Tai: rum, pineapple and orange juice, orgeat, lime and a dark rum float with an orchid on top, the drink the hotel bar hands you on day one. Fruitier than Vic's original, and honest about it.
taglineWords: out of office, into the lagoon

concepts.reading: A girls' night in is pink, creamy and fun, the Lava Flow: a strawberry purée "lava" swirled into a banana-and-coconut colada, blended, photogenic and low-effort.
garnish: a strawberry and a pineapple wedge
taglineWords: spill the tea, sip the lava

concepts.reading: The nineteenth hole: a tiki Arnold Palmer, black tea and lemonade made from scratch with honey, lifted by a lightly aged rum and a little falernum. Long, cold and clubhouse-polite.
taglineWords: a mulligan in a tall glass

concepts.reading: Derby day is the mint julep's day: a tiki-fied julep of bourbon with falernum, a little demerara and a mountain of mint over crushed ice in a frosty silver cup. Spirit-forward, cold and very green on top.
garnish: a big bouquet of mint, slapped
powdered sugar dusted over the mint
taglineWords: the run for the roses goes tropical

concepts.reading: The end of summer is bittersweet: ripe late-summer peach and passion fruit with a bitter Campari edge, a Jungle Bird cousin, sunset-colored and a little wistful.

A rare night off from the kids: something genuinely grown-up and celebratory, the Port Light (bourbon, passion fruit, honey and lemon, from Columbus's Kahiki), a little strong and very adult, savored before the babysitter's clock runs out.
taglineWords: the babysitter is on the clock

concepts.reading: A midlife crisis wants something loud, red and fast, with a wink: cherry, passion fruit and Jamaican rum with a flaming lime shell on top. Flashy like the convertible, tasty enough to justify it.
garnish: a cherry on a sword pick
taglineWords: young at heart, red in the glass

concepts.reading: Brennan's (New Orleans, 1951) sauté: banana in butter, brown sugar and cinnamon, flamed with dark rum and banana liqueur, over vanilla ice cream. Read it as banana + caramelized sugar + cinnamon on an aged-rum spine. Cold: a stirred banana-rum old fashioned or a short creamy sour; hot or flamed only if asked. The banana must come from banana liqueur or real banana, the caramel from demerara syrup and dark rum, never from blue/green liqueurs or citrus-forward juice.

Florida Keys pie: Key lime juice, sweetened condensed milk, egg yolk, graham-cracker crust, whipped cream. A tart-creamy sour: rum (or vanilla-leaning rum), lots of lime, a vanilla/cream note and a graham-crust echo (cinnamon, honey, demerara). Egg white or coconut cream gives the custard body without curdling cream. Pale cream-green, never neon green.
taglineWords: like a slice from the Keys

concepts.reading: A colada by definition: pineapple and coconut must both be present (pineapple juice + cream of coconut), plus a cake note (vanilla, a little butter-caramel from aged rum). Blended or shaken creamy. Never deliver a 'colada' without both coconut and pineapple.

Caramelized brown sugar, butter, pineapple rings and a maraschino cherry on vanilla sponge. Pineapple + caramel + cherry: aged rum, pineapple, demerara, a touch of maraschino or Heering. Stirred or shaken short; not creamy.

Coconut custard, whipped cream, toasted coconut and a buttery crust. Coconut-forward and creamy with vanilla; a little aged rum for toastiness. Colada structure without needing pineapple (call it a cream, not a colada, if pineapple is absent).
Coconut with Maillard depth: coconut plus caramel/nutty aged rum and a pinch of salt; demerara rather than white sugar. Works in a colada or a stirred coconut-washed old fashioned.

Hawaiian coconut-milk pudding set with arrowroot (now cornstarch), served at every lūʻau. Clean coconut milk, light sugar, no spice: a gentle coconut-milk colada or flip, lightly sweet, with a touch of vanilla.
taglineWords: for the end of the lūʻau

concepts.reading: Mexican horchata: soaked rice, cinnamon, vanilla, sugar, sometimes almonds; served icy. A creamy cinnamon-rice cooler: cinnamon syrup + orgeat (stands in for rice/almond body) + milk or coconut milk + a light or aged rum (or reposado). No citrus beyond a twist; no fizz.
taglineWords: poured over crushed ice like at the mercado

concepts.reading: Orange sherbet over vanilla ice cream. Orange + vanilla + cream, gently sweet, barely tart: orange juice and orange curaçao or Licor 43 (vanilla-citrus) with cream or ice cream, light rum. Keep lime minimal; never pink or red.
taglineWords: like the ice-cream truck in July

concepts.reading: Graham cracker, milk chocolate, campfire-toasted marshmallow. Chocolate (crème de cacao, a dash of mole bitters) + vanilla/honey (graham) + smoke (Demerara rum, or a mezcal or Islay rinse) + marshmallow (egg-white foam, torched if possible). Stirred short or as a creamy flip; never fruity.

Espresso-soaked ladyfingers, mascarpone, cocoa, often Marsala or rum. Coffee + cocoa + cream, a little boozy: aged rum or brandy, coffee liqueur, cold espresso, a cream float dusted with cocoa (layered). Sweet but not cloying.
taglineWords: 'pick me up', as the name says

concepts.reading: Tangy cream-cheese custard with a graham crust: lemon (tang), vanilla, egg-white body, a hint of cinnamon/honey for the crust. A rich lemon sour, not a milkshake.
Lemon curd and toasted meringue: lemon-forward sour with a thick egg-white cap, vanilla, light rum or gin (Vic used lemon freely). Bright, tart-sweet, pale yellow.

Pumpkin custard with cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, clove (and allspice). Pumpkin itself is missing from the vocabulary, so carry the pie through spice + cream + brown sugar: aged rum, allspice dram, cinnamon syrup, demerara, cream or a whole-egg flip, grated nutmeg. Autumn-warm, not citrusy; a hot version is welcome.
taglineWords: for the first cold night of fall

concepts.reading: Baked apple, cinnamon, brown sugar, buttery crust. Apple brandy and apple juice/cider are the honest carriers; cinnamon syrup, demerara, a dash of Angostura and lemon for tartness. Cold as a punch or buck, or hot like a mulled toddy.

Fair-food apple dipped in caramel (or red cinnamon candy for a candy apple). Apple brandy + apple juice + caramel (demerara, aged rum). For 'candy apple', redden with grenadine and add cinnamon heat; for 'caramel apple', stay amber.

Toasted pecans in brown-sugar/corn-syrup custard. Pecan is missing from the vocabulary; carry it with bourbon + maple/demerara + a nutty fortified wine (amontillado) or a little hazelnut liqueur. Stirred, rich, Southern.

Banana, vanilla/chocolate/strawberry ice cream, pineapple and chocolate sauce, whipped cream, cherry. A blended banana colada with chocolate and strawberry accents and a cherry on top; dessert-sweet, low acid.
Brown-butter banana loaf with walnuts and cinnamon: banana liqueur + aged rum + demerara + cinnamon + a nutty note (orgeat, amontillado). Stirred or a short flip; not fruity-bright.

Puerto Rico's Christmas drink: coconut cream and coconut milk, condensed and evaporated milk, Puerto Rican rum, cinnamon, nutmeg, clove, vanilla; chilled, served in small glasses. Creamy coconut-spice, no citrus. A colada-family cream drink, small pour.
Sponge soaked in three milks with vanilla and cinnamon; dulce de leche is milk caramel. Creamy vanilla-caramel: half-and-half + demerara + vanilla, aged rum or brandy, a cinnamon dusting.

Egg custard under burnt-sugar caramel. Vanilla + caramel + egg richness: aged rum, Licor 43 (Spain's flan partner), demerara, whole egg or egg white + cream, a bitter-sweet edge from caramelized sugar (a dash of Angostura).

Cooked sugar and butter, often salted. Demerara/Jamaican rum molasses notes + demerara syrup + a pinch of salt (saline); butterscotch adds butter (hot buttered rum batter, if hot). Stirred or short and creamy.
Chocolate dessert: crème de cacao and mole bitters on an aged/dark rum base, vanilla, cream for fudge texture; hot cocoa means hot (milk + cacao + rum). No tropical fruit juice.
Chocolate, kirsch-soaked cherries and whipped cream. Cherry Heering (or maraschino for kirsch-like dryness) + crème de cacao + aged rum or brandy, cream float optional.
Coconut, milk chocolate, almond: cream of coconut + crème de cacao + orgeat over light/aged rum, shaken creamy. Coconut-forward, sweet, no citrus.
Hazelnut + chocolate spread: hazelnut liqueur + crème de cacao + aged rum + a splash of cream; stirred or creamy.

Lunchbox sandwich: roasted peanut + grape/strawberry jelly. Peanut is missing from the vocabulary (peanut orgeat or peanut-butter-washed bourbon would be the honest carrier); approximate the nut with orgeat/amontillado and the jelly with raspberry syrup or crème de cassis, on bourbon. A short sour or stirred drink; never creamy-sweet mush.

Peanut + chocolate (+ caramel for Snickers). Peanut is missing; nearest honest stand-ins are orgeat/amontillado for nuttiness with crème de cacao and bourbon or aged rum, salted. Flag the substitution in the explanation.

Molasses, ginger, cinnamon, clove, allspice: blackstrap/dark rum + ginger syrup + allspice dram + cinnamon; a buck if fizzy, a toddy if hot, stirred if short. Speculoos leans caramel-cinnamon rather than ginger.
Dried fruit, citrus peel, brandy and spice: PX sherry or ruby port + brandy/aged rum + allspice dram + orange curaçao; stirred, or hot as a punch.

Fried dough in cinnamon sugar, dipped in thick chocolate. Cinnamon-forward, vanilla, a little chocolate and a fried-dough/caramel note: cinnamon syrup + aged rum or reposado + crème de cacao accent + cream optional.
Cinnamon, brown butter, vanilla icing: cinnamon syrup + vanilla + aged rum, creamy or stirred; a buttery note (hot buttered rum batter) if hot.
Phyllo, walnuts/pistachios, honey syrup with orange blossom and cinnamon. Honey + nut (orgeat) + orange-flower water + cinnamon on aged rum or brandy; lemon keeps it from cloying.

The 'birthday cake' flavor is vanilla + butter + a whisper of almond, with sprinkles. Vanilla syrup + orgeat (almond) + cream or egg white, light rum, a sparkling top for celebration. Sweet but balanced with a little lemon.
Southern hummingbird cake: banana, pineapple, pecans, cinnamon, cream-cheese frosting (carrot cake shares the spice and often the pineapple). Banana + pineapple + cinnamon + nutty, creamy finish.
Ripe peach with cream (or cobbler spice). Peach liqueur + apricot/peach nectar + bourbon or aged rum, cream or egg white; cobbler adds cinnamon/brown sugar; melba adds raspberry.
Fresh strawberry with cream and vanilla: muddled/blended strawberry, vanilla, cream or ice cream, light rum. Pink, soft, low acid.

Hot chocolate: served hot. Milk (half-and-half) + crème de cacao + a dash of mole bitters on aged or dark rum; Mexican hot chocolate adds cinnamon and a little chile; champurrado is masa-thickened. A Hot Tiki mug drink, not a cold shake.

Kona, the Big Island's coffee: bright, low-bitterness, nutty. Tiki already has a coffee lineage (Don's and Vic's Coffee Grog, often flamed; the Mai-Kai's coffee drinks). Coffee + aged/Demerara rum + spice (cinnamon, clove, nutmeg) + a buttery-honey note; hot or iced.

A coffee kick in a cocktail: cold espresso or cold brew + coffee liqueur + aged rum, shaken hard for crema-like foam, served up. Tiki angle: a little falernum or cinnamon. Low acid; not creamy unless asked. 'Espresso martini' is a named drink: riff it with rum rather than claim the name.

Strong drip coffee (often robusta, sometimes with chicory) over sweetened condensed milk, iced. Coffee + creamy-sweet; aged rum, coffee liqueur, half-and-half + rich syrup to approximate the missing condensed milk. Egg coffee (Hanoi cà phê trứng) adds a whipped yolk cap.

Café de olla: coffee brewed with piloncillo and cinnamon in a clay pot. Carajillo (Spain/Mexico): espresso with Licor 43. Coffee + cinnamon + dark sugar; reposado tequila or aged rum; Licor 43 for carajillo.

New Orleans café brûlot: coffee with brandy and orange curaçao flamed with orange peel, clove and cinnamon (Antoine's, 1890s, a Prohibition-era cover story). Tiki answered with flaming Coffee Grogs. Hot, flamed tableside, spiced orange-coffee.
Vanilla ice cream 'drowned' in espresso. A small scoop + hot espresso + aged rum or amaretto; serve short, creamy, bittersweet.

Cha yen: strong black tea brewed with star anise, cardamom, vanilla (and tamarind/orange-blossom in some blends), sweetened with sugar and condensed milk, topped with evaporated milk over ice; its vivid orange is food dye. Black tea + vanilla + anise-spice + creamy-sweet; Batavia arrack or aged rum suits tea. Star anise, cardamom and condensed milk are missing: five-spice syrup gives the anise, half-and-half + rich syrup the milk.

Masala chai: black tea simmered with milk, sugar, cardamom, ginger, cinnamon, clove, black pepper. Tea + warm spice + milk. Cardamom is missing; build from black tea + ginger + cinnamon + clove (five-spice for depth), aged rum; hot by default, iced if asked. 'Dirty' means a shot of espresso.

Whisked powdered green tea: grassy, vegetal, umami-bitter, often with milk and a little sugar. The vocabulary has no matcha or green tea (missing ingredient); without it, deliver the profile honestly (agricole for grass, coconut milk, honey) and do NOT fake the green color with melon or blue + yellow mixes.
Iced tea (with lemonade for an Arnold Palmer; heavily sweetened for Southern sweet tea). Long, refreshing, lemon + tea; bourbon or aged rum, peach optional for the South.
Lemon, sugar, water; pink lemonade adds a red berry. Long, bright, low-proof punch: lemon + syrup + soda or water, light rum or gin; pink via raspberry or strawberry, not grenadine overload.

Hawaii's passion-orange-guava juice (Haleakalā Dairy, Maui, 1971); Trader Sam's Uh-Oa! uses it. Equal-ish parts passion fruit, orange and guava: a pink-orange resort punch, sunny and juicy, light rum + a darker float.
taglineWords: like a carton from a Maui lunch tray

concepts.reading: Disney's pineapple soft serve (Enchanted Tiki Room/Adventureland). Pineapple + vanilla + creamy-frozen: blended pineapple, vanilla ice cream or coconut cream, light rum (the parks sell it with rum at resort bars). Frozen, pale yellow; a 'float' is pineapple juice with the whip on top.

Hawaiian shave ice: snow-fine ice with tropical syrups (strawberry, lilikoʻi, guava, li hing mui), sometimes a 'snow cap' of condensed milk and a scoop of ice cream or azuki beans underneath. Frozen, fruity, colorful but pastel. Use li hing mui syrup or guava/passion fruit; if a 'rainbow' is asked, layer colors rather than mixing them into brown.
taglineWords: from a North Shore shave-ice stand

concepts.reading: Crack seed: Chinese-Hawaiian salted, sweet-sour dried plum; li hing mui powder rims Mai Tais and coats pineapple and gummy bears in Hawaii. Chamoy (Mexico) descends from the same preserved-plum idea. Salty-sweet-tart: li hing mui syrup + lime + pineapple, a li hing rim.

Portuguese fried dough rolled in sugar (Leonard's, Honolulu, 1952), sometimes filled with haupia, custard or guava. Vanilla + fried-dough caramel + sugar, guava or coconut filling optional: creamy-light, sweet.

Hawaii's buttery nut (often chocolate-covered). Macadamia liqueur/orgeat is missing; carry it with orgeat + a buttery/vanilla note + aged rum, crème de cacao for the chocolate version. Creamy or stirred.

Savory island food: smoke (kālua pig from the imu), teriyaki sweet-salt, pineapple, ginger, scallion. The drink should be a food partner, not a gimmick: pineapple + ginger + a smoky or funky rum + saline; not creamy, not dessert-sweet.
Thai dessert: ripe mango, glutinous rice in sweet salted coconut milk, toasted mung beans/sesame. Mango + coconut + a pinch of salt; soft and rich, low acid. A coconut-mango colada with saline.

Mexican street fruit: mango (or pineapple) with chile-lime salt, chamoy. Mango + chile + lime + salt: tequila or mezcal, mango nectar, Ancho Reyes or fresh jalapeño, saline, a chile-salt rim; mangonada is frozen.

Thai aromatics: coconut milk, lemongrass, makrut lime, galangal, chili, Thai basil. Savory-aromatic coconut sour: coconut milk + lime + fresh ginger + basil + a little chili, light rum or agricole. Lemongrass and makrut lime are missing ingredients.

Filipino 'mix-mix': shaved ice, evaporated milk, ube halaya, leche flan, coconut strings, jackfruit, sweet beans, banana. Frozen, creamy, coconut-banana-vanilla. Ube (purple yam) is missing: without it the drink is cream-colored, and purple must never be faked with blue curaçao + grenadine.

Southeast Asian pandan leaf: grassy-vanilla, 'basmati' aroma, almost always with coconut (kaya jam, pandan chiffon). Pandan is missing; agricole (grassy) + vanilla + coconut approximates it. Green only with real pandan.

Rose-lychee-raspberry (Pierre Hermé's Ispahan) or Turkish delight (rose, lemon, sugar). Floral-fruity, delicate: lychee liqueur/syrup + raspberry + a whisper of rose (missing; orange-flower water is the nearest floral water in the vocabulary), lemon, light rum or gin. Pale pink, never heavy.

Spun sugar (usually pink vanilla-berry or blue raspberry). Read as sweet, light, playful; deliver a balanced pink fruit punch with vanilla and berry and enough lime to stay a drink, not a syrup. Garnish (literal floss) is the theatre.
Mouth-puckering candy: very tart, sweet-fruity. A sharp sour: extra lime or lemon, fruit syrup, light rum; sweetness kept moderate so the sourness reads. Sour apple = apple + lime, not melon liqueur.
Fruit-flavored chewy candy: red berry/cherry/watermelon, sweet. Juicy red fruit punch with real fruit (strawberry, raspberry, watermelon) and lime, light rum; sweet but balanced.

Hot cinnamon candy: cinnamon + capsaicin-like heat + red color. Cinnamon syrup + Ancho Reyes or a sliver of chili, grenadine/hibiscus for red, aged or spiced rum. 'Fireball' is a brand: read the flavor, never the name.
Anise/licorice candy: pastis or absinthe (more than drops, still restrained), Galliano for vanilla-anise, dark rum; black licorice reads dark.

Soda-fountain floats: root beer (sassafras/wintergreen, vanilla, licorice) or cola over vanilla ice cream. Root beer is missing; build cola + vanilla + a drop of anise (pastis) + allspice, aged rum, a scoop or cream float. Cherry cola adds Heering.
Orange soda: bright orange + fizz + sweet. Orange juice + orange curaçao + soda, light rum; a tall, sunny cooler.
Soda-fountain shake: ice cream + milk, blended, thick. Vanilla ice cream + aged rum + one flavor accent; frozen colada structure, modest proof.

Frozen fruit ice: bright, light, fruit-forward, tart-sweet. A frozen daiquiri structure with real fruit (passion fruit, mango, strawberry, watermelon), low proof, no dairy (sherbet may have a little).
Mixed tropical fruit (ambrosia adds coconut and marshmallow). A bright multi-fruit punch: pineapple, orange, passion fruit, a little banana or cherry; long and juicy, still balanced with lime.

Elvis's tiki moment is the film Blue Hawaii (1961), shot partly at the Coco Palms on Kauaʻi, plus Girls! Girls! Girls! (1962) and Paradise, Hawaiian Style (1966). The Blue Hawaii cocktail (Harry Yee, Hilton Hawaiian Village, 1957) predates the film by four years. Read Elvis as a 1960s resort tropical: pineapple, light rum, a little banana from his peanut-butter-and-banana sandwich, glamour. Blue only as a nod; if blue curaçao goes in, keep the rest clear or pale (pineapple turns it teal; orange or grenadine turns it murky).

Gilligan's Island (CBS 1964–67): seven castaways from the S.S. Minnow's 'three-hour tour', coconut-everything gadgets from the Professor. Read it as goofy, coconut-forward, rum-and-pineapple castaway comfort: a simple colada or rum punch served in a coconut. Light-hearted, crowd-pleasing, not too strong.

Magnum, P.I. (CBS 1980–88, Oʻahu): Thomas Magnum lives in the guest house of Robin's Nest, runs up a tab at the King Kamehameha Club, sparring with the very British Higgins and his Dobermans Zeus and Apollo. Read it as an easygoing 1980s Hawaiian resort Mai Tai with a British wink: Royal Hawaiian-style Mai Tai flavors (rum, lime, orgeat, curaçao, a pineapple-orange note) and a touch of something Higgins would approve of (black tea or sherry).

Hawaii Five-O (CBS 1968–80; reboot 2010–20): Jack Lord's crisp, no-nonsense Steve McGarrett, 'Book 'em, Danno', the surf-crashing title theme (Morton Stevens). Read it as a sharp, brisk, confident drink: strong, tart, clean; a Daiquiri- or Mai Tai-shaped sour served fast and cold, no frills.

Jimmy Buffett's Gulf-and-Western: 'Margaritaville' (1977), 'Cheeseburger in Paradise' and 'Volcano' (1978–79), 'Boat Drinks', and Alan Jackson's 'It's Five O'Clock Somewhere' (2003). Read it as Key West beach-bar ease: frozen or on the rocks, lime and salt, tequila or rum, sweet-tart and uncomplicated. A frozen tequila or rum sour, not a Margarita by name. 'Margaritaville' is a trademark; never use it as a drink name.

Walt Disney's Enchanted Tiki Room (Disneyland, 23 June 1963): singing Audio-Animatronic birds, chanting tiki poles, flowers, and the Dole Whip stand outside. Read it as joyful, family-bright and pineapple-centric: Dole-Whip-like pineapple-vanilla, colorful birds, flowers. Pineapple vessel or bird mug; light proof.

Trader Sam's Enchanted Tiki Bar (Disneyland Hotel 2011; Polynesian Village Resort 2015): drinks that trigger room effects. Uh-Oa! (bowl for two): dark and light rum, 'Gorilla Grog', P.O.G., grapefruit, cinnamon, set aflame; Krakatoa Punch: spiced and aged rum, orgeat, hibiscus, the volcano erupts; Shipwreck on the Rocks: bourbon, agave, lemon, mint, a storm rolls in. Read it as theatrical, shareable, effect-driven tiki with Jungle Cruise puns.
taglineWords: the room erupts when you order it

concepts.reading: The Disneyland ride (1967) and the films (2003–): rum-soaked swashbuckling, Tortuga, 'Why is the rum gone?'. Read it as rum-forward and nautical: a navy-rum grog or a spiced punch, dark and molasses-y, lime-honest, a barrel mug; strong enough to deserve the joke.

Bond's tropics: Ian Fleming wrote every novel at Goldeneye, his Jamaican house at Oracabessa; Dr. No (1962) was shot in Jamaica, Thunderball (1965) in the Bahamas, Live and Let Die (1973) partly in Jamaica. Bond drinks are cold, dry and precise. Read it as a sleek, spirit-forward Jamaican-rum drink: shaken and served up (Daiquiri structure) or stirred with Lillet (a Vesper wink), low sugar, an allspice (Jamaican pimento) whisper.

Miami Vice (NBC 1984–89): pastel linen, Ferrari Daytona, neon Art Deco. There is also a real drink called the Miami Vice (a frozen Piña Colada layered with a Strawberry Daiquiri). Read the show as pink-and-white layering: a frozen colada base with a strawberry daiquiri layer, flamingo-pink and white. Never name it 'Miami Vice' unless it is the riff.

The decline era's party drinks: Midori (launched at Studio 54 in 1978), blue curaçao, Malibu, peach schnapps, frozen everything. Lean into the fun with fresh citrus and real juice so an expert won't wince: melon or peach with pineapple and lime, sparkling top. Neon green only if melon liqueur is actually in it.

The Brady Bunch's 1972 Hawaii three-parter (Season 4: 'Hawaii Bound', 'Pass the Tabu', 'The Tiki Caves'): Bobby finds a 'bad-luck' tiki idol, Greg wipes out surfing, a tarantula, and Vincent Price as an archaeologist. Read it as kitsch 1970s family-vacation tiki with a playful curse: bright resort punch, passion fruit and pineapple, a dark rum 'curse' float, kid-safe by request. Respectfully: the 'curse' is TV fiction, not Hawaiian belief.

No documented tiki link to Hitchcock (uncertain; do not invent one). Read it as suspense: a drink that reveals itself slowly, dark and handsome with a bitter twist; for 'The Birds', a nod to the Jungle Bird (Campari + dark rum + pineapple). Stirred or a bitter tiki sour, coupe or bird mug, dark.

Mid-century cool: Palm Springs, Sinatra, Mad Men, the Polynesian Pop golden age (1950s–60s). Swanky, spirit-forward, stirred; or a vintage Beachcomber sour in a Pearl Diver glass. Low gimmick, high polish.

Exotica, the soundtrack of Polynesian Pop: Les Baxter's Ritual of the Savage (1951), Martin Denny's Exotica (1957; No. 1 in 1959) with bird calls and frog croaks recorded live at the Shell Bar of Kaiser's Hawaiian Village, Arthur Lyman's vibraphone. Read it as lush, mysterious, layered golden-age tiki: Don the Beachcomber spice (allspice, honey, falernum), floral hints, two rums, moody lighting.

Martin Denny's combo at the Shell Bar (Hawaiian Village, Waikīkī): playful bird calls and frog croaks over lounge piano and vibes. Read as bright, playful, birdsong-floral: a light rum sour with passion fruit, a floral lift, a bird mug if available.

Les Baxter's orchestral exotica (Ritual of the Savage, 1951): lush, cinematic, dark strings. Read as rich and dramatic: dark and Demerara rums, spice, a moody bitter edge; a heavyweight. (Avoid 'savage' in any drink name.)

Arthur Lyman, Denny's former vibraphonist, whose own group played Waikīkī (albums Taboo, 1958). Read as shimmering and crisp: a bright, effervescent swizzle or a sparkling-topped rum sour, cool mallet tones.
Don Ho's 'Tiny Bubbles' (1966), the Waikīkī showroom era. Read as effervescent and charming: pineapple-and-rum punch with a sparkling-wine crown, easy and celebratory.

Surf rock (1961–64): Dick Dale's 'Misirlou', the Chantays' 'Pipeline', the Surfaris' 'Wipe Out', the Beach Boys. Fast, bright, reverb-drenched. Read as a sharp, salty, energetic highball or swizzle: lime, ginger, salt air, quick to drink.

The Beach Boys' 'Kokomo' (1988, from the film Cocktail, Tom Cruise flipping bottles in Jamaica): a fictional island 'off the Florida Keys'. Read as a carefree resort tropical, crowd-pleasing, colorful, made with showmanship; still balanced, real juice.

Rupert Holmes's 'Escape (The Piña Colada Song)' (1979). The request is a colada: pineapple + coconut are non-negotiable. Add the song's wink (rain, a personal ad, a twist ending) in the name and garnish, not by removing the coconut.
taglineWords: for getting caught in the rain

concepts.reading: SpongeBob lives in a pineapple under the sea: pineapple-forward, playful, kid-cartoon energy. Pineapple + coconut water/sea-salt hint, light and silly; zero-proof is a good default if the guest mentions kids. Serve in a pineapple. Trademark names stay out of drink names.
taglineWords: who lives in a pineapple under the sea?

concepts.reading: Disney's Moana (2016): an ocean-voyaging Polynesian story of wayfinding and the island's heart. Treat with respect: Māui is a pan-Polynesian cultural hero, not a mascot; evoke ocean and voyaging instead. Coconut, ocean-salt, green island life: coconut water, agricole (green cane), lime, a long swizzle. No deity names in the drink name.

Lilo & Stitch (2002), set on Kauaʻi, scored with Elvis songs; 'ʻohana means family'. Read as playful, blue-alien mischief with family warmth: a pineapple-coconut drink tinted blue (keep the base clear: white rum, coconut water, lime, a small pineapple share, so it stays turquoise, not green), or a shared bowl for the ʻohana.

HBO's The White Lotus (season 1 at a Maui resort, 2021; the 'Pineapple Suite' dispute). Read as luxe resort polish with a bitter edge: an elegant Mai Tai or bitter-tiki drink, expensive-tasting rums, a little Campari bitterness under the beauty.

The Love Boat (ABC 1977–86) and cruise-ship tropicals: Isaac pouring at the bar, romance at every port. Read as sweet, pink, celebratory, sea-breezy: a resort punch with guava or strawberry, sparkling top, served pool-deck style.
taglineWords: at the next port of call

concepts.reading: Fantasy Island (ABC 1977–84): guests arrive by seaplane and their fantasy is granted. Fitting for a prayer-driven generator: honor the wish literally where it names flavors; otherwise a lush, floral, golden welcome drink with orchids.

Hemingway in Havana and Key West: the Floridita's Papa Doble (double rum, lime, grapefruit, maraschino, no sugar), Bimini fishing, the Pilar. Read as dry, tart, strong, grapefruit-maraschino-lime; frappé texture. Avoid naming it 'Hemingway Daiquiri' or 'Papa Doble' unless it is that riff.
taglineWords: for a long afternoon on the Gulf Stream

concepts.reading: Jurassic Park (1993, filmed largely on Kauaʻi): jungle, giants, a mosquito in amber. Read as a big, jungle-dark, amber drink: aged rums glowing amber, bitter-herbal jungle edge, a heavyweight Zombie-scale pour if they want monsters.

King Kong (1933): Skull Island, jungle and a giant ape. Read as banana-forward jungle heavyweight: banana liqueur and funky Jamaican rum, dark molasses, a big tiki mug; strength high but balanced with lime.
taglineWords: the eighth wonder of the world

concepts.reading: Indiana Jones (1981–): jungle temples, the golden idol, Marion's Nepal bar drinking contest. Read as adventurous and gold-tinted: passion fruit and honey gold with aged rum and spice, served in a carved mug. Golden, not blue.

Thor Heyerdahl's Kon-Tiki expedition (1947), a balsa raft from Peru to the Tuamotus (it beached on Raroia), whose book and Oscar-winning documentary fed the tiki craze. Read as an ocean-crossing drink that starts in Peru and lands in Polynesia: pisco plus rum, lime, pineapple, a navigator's spice. (Kon-Tiki was also a restaurant chain; 'Kon-Tiki Mai Tai' is a catalogue drink: don't reuse the name.)

Rodgers & Hammerstein's South Pacific (Broadway 1949; film 1958): 'Bali Ha'i', 'Some Enchanted Evening', a misty island calling. Read as romantic and misty: floral, passion fruit, soft and fragrant, mid-strength; lavender-violet dusk only if a natural carrier exists (no blue + red mixing). 'Bali Hai' is also a San Diego restaurant and its Mai Tai: don't borrow the name.
taglineWords: the island calling across the water

concepts.reading: HMS Bounty (1789): Bligh's breadfruit voyage to Tahiti, Fletcher Christian's mutiny, Pitcairn Island; films 1935 and 1962. Read as navy-grog rebellion: navy rum, lime, honey, grapefruit, strong and nautical. (Breadfruit itself isn't in the vocabulary.)
taglineWords: for the wrong side of the Articles

concepts.reading: Stranded on an island: Robinson Crusoe, Cast Away (2000), the message in a bottle. Read as resourceful and elemental: coconut water, rum, lime, a little honey; drunk from a coconut. Simple: three or four ingredients.
taglineWords: with a message in a bottle

phrases: you're gonna need a bigger boat
concepts.reading: Jaws (1975): Amity Island, the shark, 'You're gonna need a bigger boat'. Shark drinks in tiki: Vic's Shark's Tooth (overproof Jamaican, lime, lemon, grenadine, soda), Tiger Shark. Read as a bracing overproof-Jamaican sour with a grenadine 'blood' drop sinking through a clear drink; big pour, or a bowl for the 'bigger boat'.
taglineWords: you're gonna need a bigger boat

concepts.reading: Pink-everything celebration (Barbie, 2023; bachelorettes). The pink must come from real carriers: guava, hibiscus, strawberry, raspberry, a little grenadine or Campari. Light, festive, sparkling; never blue anything.

Late-70s soft rock and sailing culture: smooth, sunny, unhurried. Read as a polished, lightly bitter-bright highball or a sparkling punch: Lillet or Aperol, white rum, citrus, soda; low-proof and elegant.
Jamaica's music and ease. Read as a Jamaican-rum drink with ginger and allspice, warm and unhurried: a funky rum punch or ginger-beer highball. Respect: no ganja jokes, no patois caricature in names.

Honolulu's Hotel Street tattoo era (Norman 'Sailor Jerry' Collins; swallows, anchors, 'Hold Fast'). Read as spiced, salty, navy-strong: spiced or navy rum, lime, ginger, allspice; a barrel mug. Avoid the brand name.

Kū: Hawaiian god of war, also of fishing, canoe-building and upright strength (Kūkāʻilimoku was Kamehameha I's war god). The classic tiki mug's glowering face is a Kū. Read as upright, steadfast strength: a strong, dry-ish, spirit-forward drink with weight and structure (Demerara and Jamaican rums, lime, a little spice), served in the Kū mug the guest is probably picturing. Respect: this is a deity in living Hawaiian religion and culture. Read the domain the god governs, never caricature the god, and keep the god's name out of the drink name and out of jokes ('angry god', 'sacrifice', 'virgin').

Lono: Hawaiian god of agriculture, rain, fertility, music and peace; the Makahiki season (roughly late autumn to early spring) suspended war for games, harvest tribute and celebration. Read as generous, peaceful, rain-fed abundance: a gentle, lower-proof harvest punch for sharing (banana, sugar cane, honey, citrus), long and convivial. Respect: this is a deity in living Hawaiian religion and culture. Read the domain the god governs, never caricature the god, and keep the god's name out of the drink name and out of jokes ('angry god', 'sacrifice', 'virgin').

Kanaloa (Hawaiian), cognate with Tangaroa/Tangaloa/Taʻaroa across Polynesia: god of the ocean and its depths, voyaging and, in Hawaiʻi, paired with Kāne; later linked with the octopus/squid. Read as deep-ocean: briny, dark and calm, navy or Demerara rum, a saline edge, a long swizzle cold as deep water. Respect: this is a deity in living Hawaiian religion and culture. Read the domain the god governs, never caricature the god, and keep the god's name out of the drink name and out of jokes ('angry god', 'sacrifice', 'virgin').

Kāne: Hawaiian god of creation, life, sunlight and fresh water (with Kanaloa he opened springs by thrusting a staff into rock). Read as clean and bright: fresh cane spirit, lime, coconut water, light and pure; a dawn drink. Respect: this is a deity in living Hawaiian religion and culture. Read the domain the god governs, never caricature the god, and keep the god's name out of the drink name and out of jokes ('angry god', 'sacrifice', 'virgin').

Pele: Hawaiian goddess of volcanoes and fire, whose home is Halemaʻumaʻu crater at Kīlauea. The ʻōhelo berry (a red Vaccinium, kin to cranberry) is sacred to her and offered before eating.
